Vision and Values
Vale School has five core values that we hold dear, for our students, staff, parents and wider community. These values are:
These values help us to make decisions and work together in the best possible way.
Our newly developed vision is the journey that we aspire to for our children. Our vision is a pathway for the school on its journey.
Beginning the Journey
Every child is welcomed through the Vale School doors, and from the very first moment we make them feel secure in a community that will always put them first. We want a lifetime of happy school memories to begin on day one.
Communication is at the heart of our work with our students, and building trusting, empathetic, personalised relationships is what allows us to deliver high quality care.
Our team of professionals supports each child on their unique path, providing learning and therapy that is individually tailored towards what the child needs at each and every point. We value every step forward, no matter how small. And we recognise the path isn’t always smooth, and sometimes there are steps back; we celebrate the resilience every child shows as we stretch them to develop their independence and their own ‘voice’.
The highest aspirations for our pupils drive us to support their individual growth: every moment matters.
We take our responsibility to educate seriously; our child-centered curriculum opens up exciting new avenues and pathways. As we ensure the school environment is safe, welcoming, and joyful, we never forget our goal is to support the child on their path to an enriched and fulfilling adult life. As the child leaves through the door and on into adulthood, a better quality of life awaits them because of each and every achievement they’ve made with us along the way.

Welcome from Headteacher
I'm delighted to welcome you to Vale School. We are a specialist provision situated across three sites and offering provision for a wide variety of special educational needs.
Children and families are at the heart of everything we do at Vale School and we are always striving to create a bespoke experience so that our children and young people can be the 'best they can be.' Vale School is a warm and nurturing community with a high degree of professional expertise in working with children with SEND.
We provide meaningful learning experiences for children with medical, cognitive and physical needs. Our three different sites cater for both primary and secondary students and we have an early years provision at our Lanacasterian site.
Vale School has well established links with health and education professionals and are committed to working together with these professionals to achieve the best outcomes for our children and young people. We want our children to be equipped with the skills and confidence they need to advocate for themselves in their future.
I hope you have found the information you are looking for on our website. If you would like to arrange a visit to the school to experience our Vale community for yourself, please get in touch.
Dawn Woodcock - Headteacher - Vale School
If you require a paper copy of the website there will be no charge for this. Please contact office@vale.haringey.sch.uk

Music Therapy
Music therapy at the Vale aims to support students in various ways including their social communication, emotional expression, emotional regulation and mental health needs.
Music therapy primarily involves interactive music making. This can include improvising with the therapist on instruments, singing, listening to music, learning songs, songwriting and dance and movement. Students’ responses within the sessions inform the direction and aims of the therapy, alongside their referral information.
Music therapy sessions at the Vale are tailored towards each individual students’ needs. Long- and short-term sessions are available in both individual and group settings. Music Therapists practising in the UK are required to be registered by the Health and Care Professions Council.

Primary Site
Flamingo Chicks is a multi-award-winning national charity and inclusive community that gives all children the opportunity to explore dance and movement. We champion young disabled voices and deliver pioneering activities to develop and support the confidence, creative expression and physical competencies of the children we serve. For more information about Flamingo Chicks, please see the website.
We run weekly dance classes with students at The Vale, exploring different movements, sensory props and costumes to invite children into a world of colour! Classes are based around a core theme that lasts through the term, linked with the National Curriculum, and are intertwined with a range of dance techniques to get all children moving!
Recently, former Olympic swimmer, Michael Gunning visited the school in conjunction with Flamingo Chicks.
Groundswell Arts is a Haringey Based Arts Charity with nationally recognised work and programmes that support children, young people, and their families to develop their creativity, and sense of connection and belonging to their community. In the Spring term, we will be working with children and their families at The Vale at Lancasterian to deliver our flagship music programme Sing Our Story supported by Youth Music. Families will work with Groundswell Arts Music practitioner and songwriter Emily Stratford to write and record their own songs culminating in a shared celebration of songs later this term. Therapy Team
Vale School is supported by a multidisciplinary team from the Whittington Health NHS Trust. These include: school nurses; speech and language therapists; occupational therapists; physiotherapists; educational psychologists, dieticians and input from teachers of the deaf and blind. Teaching staff work closely with this multidisciplinary team to ensure the best outcomes for the students.

Admissions
Admissions to Vale School are agreed by the Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) Panel of Haringey’s Children and Young People’s Service, advised by the Educational Psychology Service, (EPS), in negotiation with the school.
All admissions for Haringey residents are made through the Special Education Needs (SEN) of the Local Authority (LA). You can contact Central SEN Services at: 48 Station Road, London, N22 7TY. Tel: 020 8489 387. For admissions from other boroughs, the home borough SEN department will need to be contacted.
For more information about Haringey SEND admissions, please see the website. Information about the Local Authority appeal process can also be found on this website.
The school admits children from Haringey and other neighbouring boroughs. Before admission an initial assessment of the child’s learning and medical/therapeutic needs is carried out. Parents/persons with parental responsibility play an important role in this process and are invited to visit the school with their child, talk to the Headteacher or member of the Senior Leadership Team, see the class into which their child may be admitted and talk to appropriate staff.
Visits by Vale staff to the prospective pupil’s home or current placement can then be facilitated to ensure effective liaison and a smooth transfer.
For out of borough admissions, please ensure all consultations are sent to consultations@vale.haringey.sch.uk.
